content_units: This satisfies all availability constraints and avoids back-to-back meetings for every participant.
Meeting   Participants   Start   End   Duration   Why this works
Project sync   Ava, Ben, Chloe, Diego   14:30   15:15   45 min   Only strong afternoon overlap for all four
Follow-up   Ava, Ben, Chloe   15:30   16:00   30 min   Starts after a 15-minute buffer; all 3 remain available
- The   only overlap for all four   is   14:30-15:30  , so the 45-minute full-team sync must be placed there.
- That leaves   15:15-15:30   as the only buffer before the 30-minute follow-up.
- The follow-up at   15:30-16:00   keeps a gap after the sync, so no one is in back-to-back meetings.
- Chloe is only available until   15:30   in her afternoon block, so any follow-up must either:
- start   at 15:00 or earlier   if it overlaps the team sync window, which is not possible.
- Because the all-hands slot is fixed,   15:30-16:00   is the cleanest feasible sequencing with buffer.
- Times treated as same-day local time on   2026-03-18   in   America/New York  .
- “Avoid back-to-back meetings” interpreted as a preference, not a hard constraint.
Why the chosen order is best:
- Morning triple-overlap (  10:00-10:30  ) could host the follow-up, but that would split the meetings far apart.
- The chosen pair keeps both meetings in one coordinated afternoon block while still preserving a   15-minute buffer  .
- It minimizes fragmentation and is easier for the team to attend.
